definition: A ganimal, also commonly referred to as GANimal, is a hybrid animal created with generative artificial intelligence systems, such as generative adversarial networks (GANs) or diffusion models.
details: The concept was created for a website from the MIT Media Lab in 2020, where users could create ganimal images. 78,210 ganimals were generated from hybrid pairs of animal labels from BigGAN (G1) and 3,058,362,945 ganimals generated from blending G1 ganimals. The term ganimal is a portmanteau between the words GAN and animal. It is typically used to refer to a hybrid animal generated by interpolating between distinct species; the term can also refer to any AI-generated creatures that have not been identified in reality. The ganimal concept is similar to Artbreeder, an online website for blending images with AI.

explainer.lead: A ganimal is an AI-made creature, usually produced by blending the visual features of different animal species. The idea turns image generation into a playful way to explore combinations that do not exist as identified animals in reality.

tiers.eli5: Imagine mixing pictures of two animals the way you might mix two paint colors. A computer can make a new creature whose appearance sits somewhere between them. It is an invented picture, not a newly discovered animal.
tiers.practitioner: Ganimals are made by interpolating between distinct animal labels or previously generated creatures in a generative image system, with BigGAN used for the original MIT Media Lab website and diffusion models also applicable. The main pitfall is treating a visually plausible blend as evidence of a real species or a biologically meaningful hybrid; it is simply generated imagery.
tiers.paperLevel: At a conceptual level, if A and B are distinct animal labels, interpolation produces a sequence of generated images G(blend(A, B, t)) for 0 <= t <= 1, with intermediate images described as ganimals. The concept originated on an MIT Media Lab website in 2020, where 78,210 ganimals were generated from hybrid pairs of BigGAN (G1) animal labels and 3,058,362,945 more by blending G1 ganimals. The term describes generated creatures, including ones unidentified in reality, and carries no claim of biological existence.

explainer.example: Choose two different animal labels in BigGAN and interpolate from the first to the second. Each intermediate generated image is a ganimal: a visual blend of the pair rather than a photograph of a real hybrid.

usedIn.name: MIT Media Lab ganimal website
usedIn.detail: Introduced the concept in 2020 and let users create ganimal images.

usedIn.name: BigGAN
usedIn.detail: Its G1 animal labels supplied the hybrid pairs used to generate the original ganimals.

usedIn.name: Artbreeder
usedIn.detail: A similar online application of AI image blending, though not the origin of the ganimal concept.

explainer.intuition: Instead of asking a generator for one familiar animal, you ask for something between two animal categories. The result can look like a visual crossbreed, even though no biological breeding is involved.
howItWorks: Choose two distinct animal labels, or two existing ganimal images.
Blend or interpolate between them within a generative AI system.
Use a generator such as a GAN or diffusion model to produce the corresponding creature image.
Repeat with different pairs or blends to explore many invented appearances.
explainer.whyItMatters: Ganimals provide a simple, memorable demonstration of how generative models can move between learned visual categories. They also show the difference between creative image synthesis and discovering or engineering real organisms.
misconceptions: A ganimal is not a real animal created through breeding or genetic engineering.
The term is not limited to GANs; diffusion models can also generate such creatures.
A plausible-looking ganimal is not evidence that the creature exists or has been scientifically identified.

diagram.caption: A ganimal is generated by interpolating between animal categories and turning the blend into an image.
